body: ## Summary Resolves Dependabot alert #54 - High severity RCE vulnerability in `serialize-javascript`. ## Problem The `serialize-javascript` package (versions ≤7.0.2) contains a high-severity code injection vulnerability ([GHSA-5c6j-r48x-rmvq](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5c6j-r48x-rmvq)) that can lead to remote code execution. The vulnerability exists because `RegExp.flags` and `Date.prototype.toISOString()` are interpolated directly into generated output without proper escaping. **Dependency chain in this repo:** ``` webpack (5.103.0) └── terser-webpack-plugin (^5.3.11) └── serialize-javascript (^6.0.2) ← VULNERABLE ``` ## Solution Added a yarn resolution to force `serialize-javascript>=7.0.3` (the patched version), which overrides the transitive dependency. ```json "resolutions": { "tar": ">=7.5.10", "serialize-javascript": ">=7.0.3" } ``` ## Verification - ✅ `yarn why serialize-javascript` confirms version 7.0.4 is now used - ✅ All 282 tests pass - ✅ Build succeeds with webpack - ✅ Lint passes ## Related - Resolves: https://github.com/foxglove/omgidl/security/dependabot/54 - Advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5c6j-r48x-rmvq Linear Issue: [ERT-1920](https://linear.app/foxglove/issue/ERT-1920/resolve-dependabot-alerts-for-serialize-javascript-in-omgidl)

body:
This pull request introduces a new "focus shot" feature to the arcade scene, allowing users to smoothly transition the camera to specific points of interest (hotspots) and return, as well as improvements to camera path safety and model loading. It also adds a hover card UI component for arcade machines, and refactors several components to support these features.

**Camera Focus and Hotspot System:**

- Added a "focus shot" system (`FOCUS_SHOTS`) with predefined camera/target positions and UI coordinates, allowing users to click on hotspots to smoothly focus the camera on specific scene areas and return via the ESC key or UI button. The camera and look-at transitions use damped interpolation for smoothness, and edge cases are handled to avoid abrupt jumps. (`Arcade/src/App.jsx` [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2c3f5b90c481b39714adced67d49a58dfd56eb5d5819207008c34ffc23c16cedL26-R117) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-2c3f5b90c481b39714adced67d49a58dfd56eb5d5819207008c34ffc23c16cedL90-R228) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-2c3f5b90c481b39714adced67d49a58dfd56eb5d5819207008c34ffc23c16cedR238-R329) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-2c3f5b90c481b39714adced67d49a58dfd56eb5d5819207008c34ffc23c16cedR567-R650) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-2c3f5b90c481b39714adced67d49a58dfd56eb5d5819207008c34ffc23c16cedR669-R678)
- Refactored camera path logic to clamp progress to a minimum after intro, ensuring users can't scroll back before the intended starting point, and made progress handling more robust for edge cases. (`Arcade/src/App.jsx` [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2c3f5b90c481b39714adced67d49a58dfd56eb5d5819207008c34ffc23c16cedL60-R166) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-2c3f5b90c481b39714adced67d49a58dfd56eb5d5819207008c34ffc23c16cedL90-R228) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-2c3f5b90c481b39714adced67d49a58dfd56eb5d5819207008c34ffc23c16cedR238-R329)
- Introduced a `safeSamplePointAt` utility to safely sample points along camera/target splines, preventing errors if the curve is malformed or out of range. (`Arcade/src/App.jsx` [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2c3f5b90c481b39714adced67d49a58dfd56eb5d5819207008c34ffc23c16cedR12-R26) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-2c3f5b90c481b39714adced67d49a58dfd56eb5d5819207008c34ffc23c16cedR238-R329)

**Model Loading and Intro Control:**

- Added a `ModelLoadGate` component that tracks 3D model loading progress and only enables the intro animation and user controls after loading is complete, preventing premature camera movement. (`Arcade/src/App.jsx` F8250f19L351R351, [Arcade/src/App.jsxR669-R678](diffhunk://#diff-2c3f5b90c481b39714adced67d49a58dfd56eb5d5819207008c34ffc23c16cedR669-R678))

**Arcade Machine Hover Card:**

- Added a new `HoverCard` component using `@react-three/drei`'s `Html`, which displays an interactive card UI for arcade machines when hovered, with styling and click handlers. (`Arcade/src/components/HoverCard.jsx` [Arcade/src/components/HoverCard.jsxR1-R40](diffhunk://#diff-c14205d4b7fba5ea879a611481ec4b7bc1df1c0d472917072acd747e2ae9c190R1-R40))
- Threaded `machineHoverEnabled` prop through `App`, `Scene`, `ScrollShopRig`, and `ShopModel` to enable/disable hover UI based on camera focus state. (`Arcade/src/App.jsx` F8250f19L414R414, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2c3f5b90c481b39714adced67d49a58dfd56eb5d5819207008c34ffc23c16cedL334-R692); `Arcade/src/components/Scene.jsx` [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-f7356fd71f3134c229c7a30d089c3408c955ae50fe05443436e02149dfad9c97L58-R58) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-f7356fd71f3134c229c7a30d089c3408c955ae50fe05443436e02149dfad9c97L67-R67); `Arcade/src/components/ScrollShopRig.jsx` [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-47e73801a31b654fa77d04cab6c86dcb9ec7f21d3bb5eb3ccd8b503ae8a79fd1L12-R12) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-47e73801a31b654fa77d04cab6c86dcb9ec7f21d3bb5eb3ccd8b503ae8a79fd1L56-R56)

**UI and Controls:**

- Hotspot buttons are rendered at specific screen positions when the user reaches the end of the camera path, and a floating ESC button appears during focus mode for easy exit. Keyboard navigation and focus/clear logic are also handled for accessibility and smooth user experience. (`Arcade/src/App.jsx` [Arcade/src/App.jsxR567-R650](diffhunk://#diff-2c3f5b90c481b39714adced67d49a58dfd56eb5d5819207008c34ffc23c16cedR567-R650))

These changes collectively provide a more interactive and polished camera/navigation experience in the arcade scene, with robust handling for model loading, camera pathing, and user focus interactions.

body:
### Motivation
- Introduce an explicit lifecycle for habits so they can be paused, deactivated, or archived without losing historical data and to prevent inactive habits from appearing in schedules, reminders, and streaks.
- Provide server/client APIs and UI affordances for pausing/resuming and deactivating/reactivating habits to support better review and replacement flows.

### Description
- Add a DB enum and columns via migration `supabase/migrations/0166_habit_lifecycle_status.sql` to introduce `status`, `paused_at`, `paused_reason`, `resume_on`, `deactivated_at`, and `deactivated_reason` on `habits_v2` and map archived rows to `status = 'archived'`.
- Extend `Database` types in `src/lib/database.types.ts` with the new enum and fields and update demo data handling in `src/services/demoData.ts` to populate/normalize these fields.
- Implement lifecycle helpers and APIs in `src/services/habitsV2.ts` including `getHabitLifecycleStatus`, `isHabitLifecycleActive`, `pauseHabitV2`, `resumeHabitV2`, `deactivateHabitV2`, and `reactivateHabitV2`, and make `listHabitsV2` accept `includeInactive` so consumers can opt-in to inactive rows.
- Update service behaviors to respect lifecycle status: `archiveHabitV2` now sets `status = 'archived'` and clears lifecycle fields, `listHabitStreaksV2` filters to active habits, and notification scheduling (`src/services/habitAlertNotifications.ts`) skips inactive habits.
- Update UI components to surface lifecycle state and actions: `src/features/habits/HabitsModule.tsx` adds lifecycle state, action handlers, `renderHabitCard` UI for pause/resume/deactivate/reactivate, splits active/inactive lists, and uses `isHabitLifecycleActive` when determining `todaysHabits`; `src/features/habits/DailyHabitTracker.tsx` handles `pause` and `replace` review actions and adjusts the `buildAutoProgressHabit` shape to include lifecycle fields.

### Testing
- Ran TypeScript typecheck via `tsc` to validate updated types and the build succeeded.
- Ran linting (`eslint`) to ensure code style and no new lint errors and it succeeded.
- Executed the test suite with `yarn test` (existing unit tests) and all tests passed.

## Summary

- Remove `hostNetwork: true` and `privileged: true` from GKE NCCL
  TrainingRuntime, matching Excalibur non-privileged configuration
- Use NRI device injection (`devices.gke.io` annotation) for tcpxo-daemon
  GPU/DMA device access instead of privileged mode
- Replace privileged security contexts with minimal capabilities:
  `CAP_NET_ADMIN`+`CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE` for tcpxo-daemon, `IPC_LOCK` for worker
- Shift NIC names for pod networking: control NIC `eth0`, GPU NICs `eth1-eth8`
  (previously `eth1`/`eth2-eth9` with hostNetwork)
- Generate NRI device annotation dynamically from GPU count per node
  via `buildNRIDeviceAnnotation()` instead of hardcoding 8 devices
- Remove custom SSH port (`-p 2222`), use default port 22
- Update rxdm entrypoint args: `--num_nics=8 --uid= --alsologtostderr`

## Motivation

The previous runtime used `hostNetwork: true` and `privileged: true` which
caused issues on GKE clusters with extra gVNIC Network CRs. The gVNIC
network interfered with multi-NIC pod injection, causing gpu-nic-7 to be
missing (only 7 of 8 GPU NICs injected). Moving to pod networking with NRI
device injection matches the Excalibur reference configuration and avoids
the gVNIC interference while also improving security posture.

## How it works

1. Worker pods use pod networking (no hostNetwork) with multi-NIC annotation
2. NRI device injector exposes `/dev/nvidia*`, `/dev/nvidiactl`,
   `/dev/nvidia-uvm`, and `/dev/dmabuf_import_helper` to tcpxo-daemon
3. Device list is generated dynamically from `GPU_COUNT_PER_NODE`
4. SSH uses default port 22 (no `-p 2222` remapping needed without hostNetwork)
5. NCCL env vars sourced from host `nccl-env-profile.sh` (unchanged)

- [ ] Run NCCL All-Reduce validation on GKE H100 cluster (a3-megagpu-8g)
- [ ] Verify all 8 GPU NICs are injected into worker pods
- [ ] Verify bandwidth ~335 GB/s at 8 GB message size (2 nodes)

body:
## Summary

- Fix `re.PatternError: bad escape \u at position 2` when running the conductor bridge with Python 3.13+
- Change raw string `r"\1\u2022 "` to regular string `"\\1\u2022 "` in `_markdown_to_slack()` replacement pattern

## Problem

Python 3.13 promoted the `DeprecationWarning` for invalid escape sequences in `re.sub()` replacement strings to a hard `re.PatternError`. The raw string `r"\1\u2022 "` contains `\u` which is not a valid regex escape, causing the bridge to crash on every message:

```
re.PatternError: bad escape \u at position 2
```

This prevents the Slack bridge from sending any responses back to the channel.

## Fix

Replace the raw string with a regular string so that:
- `\\1` is interpreted as the regex backreference `\1`
- `\u2022` is interpreted as the Unicode bullet character `•` by Python

## Test plan

- [x] Verified on Python 3.13.12 — bridge processes messages and sends responses to Slack without errors
- [x] The replacement still produces the correct bullet character (`•`) in Slack output

body:
issue reported [here](https://forums.meteor.com/t/meteor-3-5-beta-change-streams-performance-improvements/64461/40?u=italojs)

**bug:**
When using observeChanges with a field projection, ObjectID fields were being sent to the client as raw binary buffers instead of Mongo.ObjectID instances.

**Root cause:**
The ChangeStream driver receives fullDocument with native BSON types. Passing the raw document directly to LocalCollection._compileProjection (which uses EJSON.clone internally) caused ObjectId values to be coerced to Binary buffers.

**Fix:** 
Apply replaceTypes(doc, replaceMongoAtomWithMeteor) before projecting, converting native BSON types to Meteor equivalents before _compileProjection processes the document.

This only affected the ChangeStream driver — the oplog driver re-fetches through Meteor's cursor layer which already handles type conversion.

Tests: Added regression tests for ObjectID field type preservation on initial add, insert event, and update event.

Signal ranking used a flat `score * confidence * volatility_weight` formula with no differentiation between entry quality, trend strength, volume, or volatility. Top-N selection also had no diversity guard, allowing correlated assets (BTC + ETH + SOL) to monopolize slots.

## Weighted composite scoring (`advanced_trading_optimizer.py`)

Replaces the old formula with the specified weighted composite in `rank_signals`:

```python
composite_score = (
    entry_score      * 0.6   # signal quality (0–100)
    + trend_strength * 0.2   # ADX / EMA trend alignment
    + volume_score   * 0.1   # volume confirmation
    + inv_volatility * 0.1   # min(100, 1 / volatility_pct × 100)
)
```

- `inv_volatility` computed from numeric `volatility_pct` when present; falls back to regime-string estimates (`extreme_low=90 … extreme_high=15`)
- Missing `trend_strength` / `volume_score` default to neutral `50.0` (not derived from `entry_score` to avoid circular inflation)

## Sector diversity filter (`advanced_trading_optimizer.py`)

New `_apply_diversity_filter()` and `_get_sector()` applied after sorting:

- Walks the ranked list and defers any signal whose sector is already represented, moving it to the tail
- Result: `BTC (bitcoin) + SOL (layer_1_alt) + LINK (oracles)` instead of three correlated large-caps filling the top slots
- Uses existing `crypto_sector_taxonomy.SYMBOL_TO_SECTOR`; falls back to symbol prefix parsing
- Deferred signals are flagged `metadata['diversity_skipped'] = True` — nothing is dropped; callers taking `ranked[:N]` get a naturally diversified set

## Capital rotation integration (`ai_capital_rotation_engine.py`)

- `_step3_rank_signals` now applies the same diversity filter via a module-level `_SignalWrap` adapter that bridges the dict-based signal format to the filter's attribute interface

Every cronjob run caused unnecessary disk writes regardless of whether anything had changed — the update script always downloaded and extracted the full zip, and `update_ytdlp()` always wrote a timestamp file even when yt-dlp was already current.

## `scripts/update.sh` — ETag lazy-skip
Performs a lightweight `curl -sI` HEAD request to fetch GitHub's `ETag` for the zip archive and compares it against a locally cached `.last_etag` file. Exits immediately if unchanged; proceeds with download/extract/rsync and saves the new ETag only when the repo has actually changed.

```bash
REMOTE_ETAG=$(curl -sI "$ZIP_URL" | grep -i '^etag:' | awk '{print $2}' | tr -d '\r\n"')
LOCAL_ETAG=$(cat "$ETAG_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true)

if [ -n "$REMOTE_ETAG" ] && [ "$REMOTE_ETAG" = "$LOCAL_ETAG" ]; then
    echo "✅ Nessun aggiornamento disponibile. Uscita per risparmiare attività disco."
    exit 0
fi
```

The `[ -n "$REMOTE_ETAG" ]` guard ensures a silent `curl` failure falls through to a full update rather than a false skip.

## `youtube_napoletano/downloader.py` — Conditional timestamp write
`update_ytdlp()` now captures stdout+stderr and only writes `UPDATE_TIMESTAMP_FILE` when the output confirms a successful check (`"yt-dlp is up to date"`) or an actual update (`"Updating to"`). Unrecognised output and exceptions both leave the timestamp file untouched.

## Supporting changes
- `.gitignore`: added `.last_etag`
- `tests/test_downloader.py`: added `TestUpdateYtdlp` covering all four branches of the conditional write logic

body:
## Summary
Introduces a new `HybridSolver` that combines an approximate solver (VSA) with an exact solver (Z3) to balance performance and precision. The solver adds constraints to both backends and intelligently routes queries based on whether expressions are symbolic and the nature of the operation.

## Key Changes

- **New HybridSolver implementation** (`clarirs_core/src/solver.rs`):
  - Generic struct combining approximate and exact solver backends
  - Implements full `Solver` trait with intelligent fallback logic
  - For satisfiability checks: tries approximate first, falls back to exact if needed
  - For symbolic expressions: consults exact solver for correctness-critical operations
  - For concrete expressions: uses fast approximate solver
  - Evaluation methods (`eval_bool_n`, `eval_bitvec_n`, etc.) try approximate first and validate with exact

- **DynSolver enum extension** (`clarirs_py/src/dynsolver.rs`):
  - Added `Hybrid` variant wrapping `HybridSolver<VSASolver, Z3Solver>`
  - Introduced `dispatch!` macro to reduce boilerplate in trait implementation
  - Updated all solver methods to support the new variant
  - Extended `unsat_core()` to support hybrid solvers (delegates to Z3 backend)

- **Python API support** (`clarirs_py/src/solver.rs`):
  - New `PyHybridSolver` class exposing hybrid solver to Python
  - Integrated into solver cloning, reconstruction, and factory methods
  - Updated solver type detection to recognize "Hybrid" string representation
  - Hybrid solver properly participates in unsat core tracking

- **Test coverage**:
  - Added `test_hybrid_solver_concrete()` validating basic hybrid solver operations

## Implementation Details

The hybrid solver uses a strategic approach:
- **Constraints**: Added to both backends (approximate may ignore, exact tracks)
- **Satisfiability**: Approximate solver's "definitely unsat" is trusted; otherwise exact is consulted
- **Symbolic checks**: Non-symbolic expressions use fast approximate path; symbolic use exact for correctness
- **Evaluation**: Approximate results are preferred if available; exact solver validates or provides fallback

body:
Checklist for reviewer:

When adding a new derived dataset:
- [ ] Ensure that the data is not available already (fully or partially) and recommend extending an existing dataset in favor of creating new ones. Data may be available in [bigquery-etl repository](https://github.com/mozilla/bigquery-etl), [looker-hub](https://github.com/mozilla/looker-hub) or in [looker-spoke-default](https://github.com/mozilla/looker-spoke-default/tree/e1315853507fc1ac6e78d252d53dc8df5f5f322b).
- [ ] Avoid merging a PR that includes the logic of a [core metric](https://docs.telemetry.mozilla.org/metrics/index.html) or complex business logic. The recommendation is to implement core business logic in bigquery-etl. E.g. The [type of search](https://github.com/mozilla/bigquery-etl/blob/a3e59f90326816a2ecaaa3e9d5b57fe9552f7d70/sql/moz-fx-data-shared-prod/search_derived/mobile_search_clients_daily_v1/query.sql#L781).
- [ ] Avoid merging code in Looker Explores/Views that implement analysis with multiple lines of code or that will be likely replicated in the future. Instead, aim for extending an existing dataset to include the required logic, and use [Looker aggregates](https://cloud.google.com/looker/docs/aggregate_awareness) to facilitate the analysis.
- [ ] Avoid merging a PR with logic that requires validation and health checks. It is recommended to implement it in bigquery-etl for full test coverage and failure alerts.

### Motivation
- Resolve a critical authentication/state-mixing issue where an old user remained visible after logout and a different account logged in. 
- Ensure logout fully clears in-memory auth/profile state (Riverpod) so no leftover name/uid/favorites remain. 
- Remove hardcoded placeholder display strings (e.g. "Admin") and ensure displayed names come from the current user document. 
- Guarantee navigation to home happens only after the signed-in user’s Firestore profile is loaded into global state.

### Description
- Centralized sign-in/register/logout flows through the Riverpod `AuthNotifier` so `signIn`, `register` and `signInWithGoogle` return the loaded `UserModel`, invalidate `userModelStreamProvider`, and `signOut` clears notifier state and invalidates the user stream. (changes in `lib/providers/auth_provider.dart`) 
- `ProfileNotifier` now listens to `authStateProvider` uid changes and will clear state to `null` on sign-out and load the correct user profile when the uid changes, preventing stale profile leakage. (changes in `lib/providers/profile_provider.dart`) 
- Login and register screens use `authNotifier` flows and only navigate (`context.go('/main')`) after the notifier returns a non-null `UserModel`; Google flows use the notifier as well. (changes in `lib/screens/auth/login_screen.dart` and `lib/screens/auth/register_screen.dart`) 
- Replaced direct `FirebaseAuth.instance.signOut()` calls in settings screens with the notifier `signOut()` so both Firebase and in-memory state are reset consistently. (changes in `lib/screens/settings/settings_screen.dart` and `lib/screens/profile/fiyatradar_settings.dart`) 
- Introduced `preferredDisplayName` (and `emailPrefix`) logic on `UserModel` to choose display name in order: `username`, `name`, then email prefix; updated profile, personal-info and home UI to use this dynamic value instead of hardcoded placeholders. (changes in `lib/models/user_model.dart`, `lib/screens/profile/personal_info_screen.dart`, `lib/screens/profile/profile_screen.dart`, `lib/screens/home/home_screen.dart`)
